notes: Stores the Js5Archive (aJs5Archive_458). If non-null, reads the archive's group/file count via `aJs5Archive_458.method414(-1) - 1` and calls `aJs5Archive_458.method407(0, i_6_)` - looks like validating/priming the archive with its own last-valid index (typical 'preload/validate archive index table' step). Wraps everything in a try/catch that rethrows as TextureLoadException with a formatted 'iba.<init>(...)' message (iba = this class's obfuscated JODE name), which is only useful for crash diagnostics. `sceneProjector` and `i` are captured/used only in the exception message, never stored as fields; `i` in particular is not used for any real logic in this constructor.

Core loader entry point: looks up a cached CacheArchiveIndex for `id` in the LRU cache (aLruByteCache_460, keyed by `id.toLong()`); if present, returns it. Otherwise reads the raw group data for `id` from the Js5Archive (aJs5Archive_458.method410(-1860, SpriteComponent.method200(-107, id), AbstractFrameBufferSurface.method3013(id, bool))), constructs a new (possibly empty) CacheArchiveIndex, decodes it via CacheArchiveIndex.method1069/decode if data was found, caches it, and returns it. This matches the classic RS 'archive index/config table' lazy-load-and-cache pattern (analogous to loading an Enum/Struct config archive entry by id). The `bool` param is passed through to method3013 (an unrelated helper) but is never referenced directly inside this method body; every call site (ChatCommandProcessor.kt, ItemNameResolver.kt, Player.kt) passes literal `true`, so its real effect could not be confirmed from this file alone.

Companion/static: if `contextId` equals a sentinel NamedIdRecord-derived hash (IntHashSetStatics...method1815(-32350)), forces itemId to -1. If the resulting itemId differs from the cached GlShaderProgramHandle.anInt4179: when itemId != -1, looks up the item's ItemDefinition (via aItemDefinitionLoader_3147) and its cursor sprite (method1610); if a cursor sprite exists, sets a custom mouse cursor image via VorbisOggDecoder.aPrivilegedOperationWorker_8992.method2238(width, height, 17, hotspotPoint, canvas, pixels) and caches the new itemId; when itemId == -1 and a cursor was previously set, resets to the default cursor (method2238(-1, null, ...)). This strongly resembles RS's custom-item-cursor feature (e.g. a special cursor shown while a certain item is selected/wielded). Confidence is medium because the exact semantics of the sentinel comparison for `contextId` could not be fully traced.

notes: Fills `buffer[baseOffset+start .. baseOffset+end)` with byte value 1, in chunks of 4 followed by a 0-3 byte remainder. `i_2_`/`unused` is overwritten immediately (`i_2_ = -i_1_ + i_4_ shr 2`) before any use, so its incoming value is discarded/decoy. Called only from NativeRenderNode.kt's software triangle rasterizer (dozens of call sites) always with the literal magic constant 1354705384 for `i_3_`, so the `if (i_3_ == 1354705384)` remainder-fill branch always executes in practice - not a dead branch, but the parameter itself carries no real information (equivalent to a hardcoded boolean true) rather than being a meaningful flag. Likely used to paint a coverage/stencil byte-mask for a scanline span of the rasterized triangle.

Classic round-up-to-next-power-of-two bit-twiddling routine (`i--; i|=i>>1; i|=i>>2; i|=i>>4; [i|=i>>8; i|=i>>16;] return i+1`), used throughout the codebase both for sizing Hashtables (e.g. CacheArchiveIndex.method1065/decodeOpcode) and for computing power-of-two texture width/height for GL textures (D3DTexture2D.kt, GlRenderDevice.kt, InvertTextureNode.kt, etc). Every call site in the repo passes the literal `108.toByte()` for `magicByte`, so the `if (i_5_.toInt() != 108) return 34` early-return branch is dead in practice across the entire codebase - it would truncate the calculation (skipping the >>8/>>16 shift steps, so it's only correct for inputs up to 255) and return a hardcoded 34 for any other input, but that path is never observed to be taken.
